title: Brain dopamine damage identified as cause of long COVID fatigue
summary: PET brain imaging at CAMH revealed long COVID damages dopamine-releasing neurons in the striatum, correlating dopamine loss patterns with specific symptoms: motivation loss, movement slowing, and memory difficulties. The finding opens potential treatment strategies targeting the dopamine system.
takeaways: Long COVID affects approximately 5% of global population (~2 million people in Canada)
Lower ventral striatum dopamine linked to loss of motivation
Dorsal putamen dopamine reduction associated with slower movement
Caudate putamen dopamine loss connected to memory difficulties
No current evidence-based treatments exist for long COVID

takeaways: Device combines recording, drug delivery, and stimulation in single implant

title: Magnetic Bacteria Extends C. elegans Lifespan by 43%
summary: A magnetotactic bacterium called Magnetospirillum magneticum AMB-1 extended C. elegans worm lifespan by 43.39% while protecting neurological function and intestinal integrity. takeaways: Average lifespan extended by 43.39% in C. elegans

title: GLP-1 drugs linked to nutritional deficiencies in nearly 1 in 6 children
summary: A study of 2,031 children on GLP-1 medications found that 16.8% developed a nutritional deficiency within one year, with vitamin D deficiency most common at 12.4%. Only 5% received nutritional counseling within 30 days of treatment initiation.
takeaways: 16.8% of children (nearly 1 in 6) diagnosed with nutritional deficiency within first year
Vitamin D deficiency most prevalent at 12.4%; iron and calcium also concerning for adolescent skeletal health
Only 5% received nutritional counseling within 30 days; <25% within 6 months
Liraglutide accounted for 78.6% of prescriptions; dulaglutide 10.4%; semaglutide 9.1%

title: Broken nerve-muscle signaling may explain age-related muscle weakness
summary: Researchers at the University of Missouri-Columbia identified a breakdown in nerve-muscle communication as a cause of age-related muscle weakness and sarcopenia. In animal models, targeting a protein called ClC improved muscle strength, suggesting the mechanism may be partially reversible.

Lower NaV1.4 protein levels impair muscle fiber response to nerve signals
ClC protein targeting improved muscle strength in animal models

title: Experimental Drug CS18 Shows Promise in Breaking Cancer Drug Resistance

takeaways: Targets TopBP1 protein involved in cancer growth regulation
Effective across triple-negative breast cancer, ovarian cancer, lung adenocarcinoma, and acute myeloid leukemia
Restored drug sensitivity in resistant lung cancer cells when combined with PARP inhibitors
Published in Science Advances on September 22, 2026

title: Stem cell transplants restore movement in mice after stroke
summary: Researchers at the University of Zurich transplanted human neural stem cells into stroke-damaged brains one week post-stroke, where they survived, differentiated into neurons, regenerated tissue, restored motor function, and improved blood-brain barrier integrity over five weeks.
takeaways: Transplanted cells survived and most transformed into neurons communicating with existing brain cells
Treatment restored motor function and improved blood vessels, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier integrity
Stroke affects approximately 1 in 4 adults over lifetime, with ~50% experiencing lasting disabilities such as paralysis or speech difficulty
Study addresses traditionally permanent brain damage with neural stem cell therapy

takeaways: GAE is minimally invasive outpatient procedure taking 1–2 hours

takeaways: 153,902 adults analyzed across 69 randomized controlled trials
